lesson_title: A Spider, a Termite and an Engineer
hook_text: A spider web, a termite mound and a cell phone mast have the same job description. Here it is.
clip_script: Stand on a street corner in Soweto and look around. A house. A water tank on a steel stand. A footbridge over the canal. A jacaranda with a weaver's nest. A spider web on the fence. A cell phone mast on the hill. Every one of them is a structure: parts arranged to keep a shape and carry a load. And every one does at least one of four jobs. Contain: the tank holds water. Protect: the house keeps the family dry. Support: the stand holds the tank, the mast holds antennas high. Span: the bridge crosses the canal, the web crosses the gap in the fence. Now sort them. Nature made the tree, the nest and the web. People made the rest. But people copy nature all the time: hollow reeds became steel tubes, honeycombs became stiff panels, and a termite mound's cooling channels became a shopping centre in Harare. Structures are everywhere, and from now on you will see them.
visual_style: Whiteboard street scene with each object circled and labelled with its job; a split line sorts them into natural and man-made.
mood: Observant and warm, the ordinary street turned into a lesson.
pacing: Slow pan across the street, four jobs in quick beats, sorting and the nature-copying twist to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name the job of five structures on your own street.
